1.2.0: Set up a stable computer copy with Desktop and Start or Applications menu shortcuts.
Faster Windows launches from the computer copy after the first setup.
Verify signed USB updates and preserve your existing local profiles, settings and browser downloads.
Find version details, release notes and pinning guidance in App & updates.
Refreshed application icon across the launcher, desktop and taskbar.
1.3.0: Check, download, verify, and restart with online updates from App & updates.
Public Windows and Linux downloads with signed release metadata and SHA-256 checksums.
Keep local profiles and proxy credentials on each device.
Protected release uploads and atomic publishing with GitHub Actions deployment.
Consistent browser branding across desktop, shortcuts, and the download website.
1.4.0: Choose the proxy provider for each profile and launch; provider keys are stored per device in the encrypted vault, and existing keys move over automatically (a backup of the previous vault is kept).
Site access tokens: send a secret header only to your own listed sites so your WAF or CAPTCHA can allow QA traffic.
Self-healing selectors: recorded steps keep backup locators, healed steps are flagged in results, and one click updates the scenario.
Headless runner as a Docker image and a reusable GitHub Action for CI.
Fixed online updates failing with "The update is outside the managed download directory". Install this version once by downloading it from the website; later updates work from App & updates.

After an update, a copy opened straight from a downloaded file becomes the computer copy with Desktop and Start menu shortcuts, so the next launch opens the new version; opening an older file offers the newer version.
Linux: the app now reopens after an update or when opening the computer copy (the restarted AppImage previously failed with "Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup").
Now open source under the Apache License 2.0. Desktop and menu shortcuts are updated automatically; on Windows, unpin and re-pin a taskbar pin once if it opens a second taskbar button.
1.5.0: macOS downloads for Apple silicon and Intel (macOS 12 or later). The DMGs are unsigned: allow each new download once with System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. The Mac app checks for updates and opens the download page; replace the app in Applications to update, and your profiles are kept.

Consent, accessibility and performance checks for QA automation: test a consent disclosure's wording, visibility, font size, contrast and distance from the submit button; that the consent checkbox is not pre-checked; TrustedForm, Jornaya or custom lead scripts; axe-core accessibility rules; and performance budgets, optionally with network throttling (Chromium). Results and reports list every failed check.

QA automation handles more real-world forms: actions can run inside iframes, continue in pop-up windows and upload files stored with the scenario. Recording also captures actions in frames and pop-ups, and file choices (attach the file itself before saving).

QA runs now follow HTTP redirects that stay on the scenario's approved sites, such as a form that redirects to a thank-you page, instead of blocking them. Each redirect is shown in the evidence and reports; turn off Follow redirects within approved sites to block them as before.

Bright Data, Oxylabs, Decodo and IPRoyal residential proxies are now built in next to DataImpulse. They follow each provider's official documentation but have not been tested with a live account, so the app labels them community-verified.

When it starts, the app now checks for updates (at most once a day) and shows an Update badge next to the version in the sidebar; nothing is downloaded until you choose. Turn it off in Settings → General → Check for updates on startup.
After an online or USB update on Windows and Linux, a notice confirms the new version or explains why the update did not finish, with a Retry update button.

Site access tokens: file uploads to your listed sites now include the file's contents in Chromium and WebKit, which used to send an empty file. If a file cannot be included, for example one over 25 MB, the upload is blocked and the reason is written to the app log.
Fixed QA automation runs failing to start the bundled Chromium in the Linux app; the first-run browser download in the Windows app is about 100 MB smaller.

New MCP server (qa-mcp) lets AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Cursor run geo- and device-aware QA checks on sites you allowlist. It ships with the source code and the runner Docker image, not with the desktop app.
